facts.t: A Financial Emergency has never been declared
facts.d: Article 360 has stood unused since 1950 — not even during the 1991 balance-of-payments crisis, when India pledged gold reserves to the Bank of England rather than invoke it.

facts.t: The 44th Amendment made two rights absolutely unsuspendable
facts.d: After ADM Jabalpur held that even the right to life could be suspended during Emergency, the 44th Amendment placed Articles 20 and 21 permanently beyond suspension. The judgment was formally described as seriously flawed by the Supreme Court in Puttaswamy, four decades later.

facts.t: Justice H. R. Khanna's lone dissent cost him the Chief Justiceship
facts.d: He was the only judge in ADM Jabalpur to hold that liberty survived the Emergency. He was superseded for the top job soon after, and resigned. The New York Times wrote at the time that a statue should one day be raised to him.

bank.q: With reference to a National Emergency under Article 352, consider the following statements:
s: Internal disturbance was replaced by armed rebellion as a ground by the 44th Amendment.
The Union Cabinet must recommend the proclamation in writing.
Approval requires a simple majority in both Houses within thirty days.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Approval needs a special majority — the majority of the total membership of each House and two-thirds of those present and voting.

bank.q: During a National Emergency, Article 19 is automatically suspended:
o: Only where the emergency is declared on the ground of external aggression
Only where the emergency is declared on the ground of armed rebellion
bank.e: The 44th Amendment confined automatic suspension of Article 19 to emergencies proclaimed on the ground of war or external aggression, not armed rebellion.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT an effect of a National Emergency?
o: Parliament may legislate on State List subjects
The President may alter the distribution of revenues to the States
State legislatures and executives stand dissolved
The Lok Sabha's term may be extended one year at a time
bank.e: A National Emergency makes India functionally unitary, but state legislatures and executives are not dissolved — that is the effect of Article 356, not Article 352.

bank.q: Match List I (case) with List II (holding on emergency powers):
pairs: A. State of Rajasthan v. UoI
1. Dissolving a fresh assembly on anticipated horse-trading is unconstitutional
2. President's satisfaction is reviewable if mala fide or on irrelevant grounds
3. Life and liberty were held suspendable during Emergency
4. The floor test determines majority, and courts may restore dismissed governments
bank.e: Rajasthan opened the door to review, Bommai built the modern framework, Rameshwar Prasad addressed pre-emptive dissolution, and ADM Jabalpur is the case the 44th Amendment reversed.

bank.as: President's Rule may be extended beyond one year only in limited circumstances.
bank.rs: Extension beyond a year requires either a National Emergency to be in force or a certification by the Election Commission that elections cannot be held.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — a safeguard introduced to stop the indefinite extensions common in the 1970s and 1980s.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about Article 356:
s: A Governor's report is a precondition for imposing President's Rule.
Parliamentary approval requires a simple majority within two months.
High Court powers cannot be subsumed during President's Rule.
bank.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. President's Rule can be imposed without a Governor's report, though Sarkaria recommended that any such report be a speaking document.

bank.q: All of the following have been treated as improper grounds for Article 356 EXCEPT:
o: An overwhelming defeat of the state ruling party in Lok Sabha elections
A hung assembly with no party able to form a government
Using the power merely to achieve good government
bank.e: A hung assembly is a recognised proper ground. The other three are the classic improper grounds identified by Sarkaria and Bommai.

bank.q: How many National Emergencies have been proclaimed in India?
bank.e: Three — 1962 during the Chinese aggression, 1971 during the war with Pakistan, and 1975 on the ground of internal disturbance.

bank.q: With reference to a Financial Emergency under Article 360, consider the following:
s: It may be used to direct reductions in the salaries of state government employees.
The salaries of Supreme Court and High Court judges may also be reduced.
Its duration is limited to six months at a time.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Once approved, a Financial Emergency continues indefinitely until revoked by the President — there is no periodic re-approval requirement.

bank.q: Arrange the following in correct chronological order:
bank.e: ADM Jabalpur (1976) → State of Rajasthan v. UoI (1977) → the 44th Amendment (1978) → S. R. Bommai (1994).

bank.q: A National Emergency can be revoked by a resolution of:
o: The Lok Sabha by simple majority
The Rajya Sabha by simple majority
bank.e: The 44th Amendment gave the Lok Sabha alone the power to disapprove by simple majority, and allowed one-tenth of its members to requisition a special sitting within fourteen days.

bank.as: A proclamation under Article 352 is subject to judicial review.
bank.rs: Courts may examine the adequacy of the reasons that satisfied the President.
bank.e: The Assertion is true — Minerva Mills settled reviewability — but the Reason is false. Review extends to constitutional limits, mala fides and irrelevant grounds, not to the adequacy or sufficiency of the reasons.
